transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Nora (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO), Jin-Woo (ML), Larissa (Infra), Ava (Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
- Aurelia Labs evaluating Redwood for a token-burst use case tied to real-time assistant product. Primary concerns: p95 latency under burst, concurrency limits, streaming token/sec for long-turn conversations, and data residency / SOC2.
- They want a 2-week pilot on Dedicated to validate p95 and cost; likely follow-on Private if security gates require it.

Topics covered:
- p95 targets and measurement approach
- Concurrency & connection shaping for streaming tokens/sec
- Model variants and quantization tradeoffs
- Fallback and routing policies during capacity events
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, residency

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off quick — ethan here from redwood
[00:18] Samir (Aurelia): yeah thanks, um we've got about 50 minutes, i'll let jin-woo and larissa jump in on the specifics, but main ask is: when we get a token surge, can you keep our p95 for user-facing streaming under ~300ms?
[00:35] Nora (Redwood SE): great question. quick clar — when you say streaming under 300ms, do you mean end-to-end token latency (first byte to client) or server-side generation p95?
[00:48] Jin-Woo (Aurelia): end-to-end, specifically first-byte for token streaming to the user. If i recall, that includes networking, right — but we mostly care about the inference portion being predictable.
[01:05] Luis (Redwood): correct, the slate we monitor is server generation + rtt; for on-hosted deployments we can give detailed breakdowns; for Dedicated we typically see a consistent p95 for generation, then add a network delta.
[01:22] Larissa (Aurelia): and our app runs in eu-west-1, data residency is important — we may need a private deployment if the logs cannot leave region.
[01:35] Ethan: noted. two quick things — what concurrency at peak are you planning? and what's your typical tokens/sec per session?
[01:44] Samir: we have a production estimate: 3k active sessions, but concurrent generating streams at peak maybe 200-300. token rates vary — short queries ~20-50 tokens/sec, long sessions 150+ tokens/sec for a bursty assistant.
[02:05] Nora: ok good, that gives us a baseline. for 200-300 concurrent streams on a single Dedicated 4xA100-type pool, rough numbers — depends on model size, sequence length and KV cache hit rate, but ballpark: p95 for single-token streaming often sits in the 80-250ms window with our optimized kernels for ggml-style quant or fp16. but again, many moving parts.
[02:28] Jin-Woo: model size: we're looking at running a 30B-ish open model quantized to int8 for cost. will you be supporting that?
[02:35] Nora: yes, we support quantized int8 and int4 variants; our runtime has quantization-friendly execution paths. we do see different p95 behavior — int8 may add a small decode overhead but reduces memory pressure and enables higher concurrency.
[02:48] Samir: price vs latency tradeoff is important — we could accept slightly higher p95 if cost per token drops 30% or more.
[02:56] Luis: that's where our Optimize recommendations come in — we can show batching windows, prefix caching, and token-level caching to tradeoff. for streaming, aggressive batching hurts tail latency, so we usually set a small batching window and rely on KV caching to lower compute.
[03:12] [speaker overlap / crosstalk]
[03:20] Ava (Product): can you explain KV cache briefly? sometimes our product team confuses it with LRU caching at the app layer.
[03:28] Nora: sure — KV cache stores past key/values for the attention cache per session so repeated context doesn't need re-computation; it's server-side, TTL-controlled. for conversations it can shrink compute for long contexts and reduce tokens/sec CPU. mis-transcription: sometimes shows as K V cash.
[03:45] Samir: also, we need to see p95 over 48-hour sustained bursts, not just a 5-minute test. our user patterns have diurnal spike and sudden surges.
[03:58] Ethan: totally reasonable. our standard pilot includes a 48–72 hour run; we'll ask you to upload a representative prompt set and session characteristics. we can run token traces and provide p95 histograms by model variant.
[04:13] Jin-Woo: about concurrency — will you shard across multiple model replicas or queue? we can't let requests queue more than 500ms or UX suffers.
[04:24] Nora: we use smart routing — can route by latency-first or cost-first. in Dedicated, you can pin to a pool; we autoscale within the pool for throughput but not beyond, so there are backpressure policies. we also support graceful fallback to smaller model variants to keep throughput if capacity saturates.
[04:40] Larissa: fallback worries me — what if fallback leaks data or downgrades quality unexpectedly?
[04:48] Luis: fallback is configured per-customer; quality regressions are visible in the console and you can set automatic rollback thresholds. private deployments avoid cross-customer routing entirely.
[04:59] Samir: what are typical token/sec numbers per GPU for a 30B quantized model?
[05:06] Nora: varies, but rough: 30B int8 on an A100-class GPU can do ~400-800 tokens/sec per GPU for autoregressive generation under streaming micro-batching; for low-latency streaming single-token mode you'll be at the lower end. with KV cache hit rates high you get effective tokens/sec much higher per session.
[05:28] Jin-Woo: so for 200 concurrent streams we need about 4-8 GPUs? that math seems optimistic.
[05:34] Nora: yes it's optimistic if you assume 100% packing. realistic factor: concurrency inefficiency and network overhead; i'd plan 6-10 GPUs as a safety band, or use Dedicated with burst capacity to absorb peaks.
[05:47] Ethan: and we can instrument a cost model for you — tokens/sec vs $/k tokens — and show cost for Dedicated reserved hours vs Hosted pay-as-you-go.
[05:57] Ava: do you have examples of customers who moved from Hosted to Dedicated for similar workloads?
[06:03] Ethan: yes, a couple — one moved after discovering spikes caused throttling at peak and needed reserved capacity. another moved to Private for compliance reasons after validating p95 on Dedicated. we can anonymize references.
[06:14] Samir: security: we need SAML SSO, KMS encryption at rest, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can you do that?
[06:22] Luis: yes. SAML/SSO, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations available for Dedicated and Private. audit logs can be exported to your S3 or syslog; we can provide sample schema. we'll share SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[06:36] Larissa: does Redwood persist prompts or are they ephemeral by default?
[06:40] Nora: by default logs are retained per-customer policy — for hosted there is a retention default; Dedicated and Private customers can set retention or opt out of storing prompts beyond the timeframe needed for observability. we'll note the retention options in the security doc.
[06:56] [00:07:00] Ethan: technical deep-dive: jin-woo, can you describe token length distribution for your long sessions?
[07:05] Jin-Woo: typically new chat turn 20-60 tokens, mid-session turns can be 200-800 tokens; sequences can go up to 6k tokens when we include context. KV caching is important there.
[07:18] Nora: long contexts affect memory and KV cache eviction; we advise either windowing or context summarization to keep tail latency predictable. also compilation/kernels selected change with sequence length.
[07:31] Samir: what about p95 percentile definition — do you measure on a per-token or per-request basis? we need per-first-byte and per-complete-response metrics.
[07:41] Luis: we can provide both: first-byte latency for streaming token and full-response tail. console exposes p50/p95/p99 and we can export traces for correlation with tokens.
[07:52] Ava: question about SDK — will we get client libraries for streaming and reconnect logic?
[07:58] Ethan: yes SDKs (js/python) with reconnect, resume and token streaming; we also surface token deltas for cost accounting.
[08:08] [08:18] Jin-Woo: one more — can we run a side-by-side benchmark against our in-house infra? we want apples-to-apples with identical prompts and environment.
[08:25] Nora: absolutely — we'll provide the harness. we'll need a reproducible environment (docker images, prompt seeding) and a way to upload your traces. we also encourage enabling tracing hooks for detailed kernel-level breakouts.
[08:39] Samir: what if network rtt in eu-west-1 adds 60-80ms, will that put us over 300ms?
[08:47] Luis: it can. that's why we report breakdowns. we can deploy a regional Dedicated pool closer to your region or set up Private in your VPC to minimize network hops.
[08:59] Larissa: cost question: if we reserve Dedicated, do we pay for idle capacity during off-peak? can you do burst pricing?
[09:07] Ethan: reserved capacity contracts do have baseline commit, but we offer burst credits and autoscale within the committed pool; for heavy burst patterns we recommend a blended plan — reserved baseline + elastic burst. we'll include scenarios in the pricing doc.
[09:22] [09:30] Samir: regarding fallback logic — can you demo a canary or A/B rollout that degrades to smaller model under stress but keeps conversation thread continuity?
[09:39] Nora: yes, rollout policies support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback with quality gates. for conversation continuity we maintain session affinity so fallback models still see the KV cache if compatible; if not compatible we document the regression.
[09:55] Ethan: ok quick recap and actions: we'll run a 48-hour Dedicated benchmark with your prompt sets; share SOC2 and ISO artifacts; we'll provide pricing scenarios and a recommended GPU count; schedule pilot kickoff week of Dec 14.
[10:10] Samir: good. one ask: include a token-trace showing per-token p95 and p99 and a simple cost projection per million tokens.
[10:18] Ethan: yes, we'll include that.
[10:22] Jin-Woo: small transcribe glitch: sometimes i heard K V cash, not cache — but it's clear now.
[10:28] [Crosstalk]
[10:35] Larissa: last sec governance point: if we go Private we need an offline installer or airgap option — is that doable?
[10:41] Luis: yes, we have an on-prem package used by regulated customers; that'll be part of the enterprise conversation.
[10:48] Ava: can you send a short one-pager that maps p95 targets to recommended configurations (gpu count, model variant, expected $/k tokens)?
[10:55] Ethan: will do.
[11:00] [11:10] Closing notes: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the benchmark template and security packet. feel free to reach out if you want a deeper SE-led kernel dive.

End of transcript.
